name: Gmail
description: Send and read email through the authenticated user's Gmail account.
_authNote: OAuth endpoints, scopes, client secret ref and any identity step are PLATFORM-OWNED — they live in the private clarity-api (integrations-v2/config/oauth-configs.ts), never in this public repo. This manifest only declares that the integration uses oauth2 and which tools it provides.

providedTools.description: Send an email (optionally as a reply in a thread). To send a LIST of records, bind `report.rows` to the structured data and it is delivered as a formatted table with a chart — do not flatten a list into prose.

List messages, newest first; supports paging. Each result already carries id, thread_id, sender, sender_email, sender_name, subject, date and snippet. Bind them directly. Do NOT add a step to extract those fields; they are not in the message body.

messages.description: Rows of {id, thread_id, sender, sender_email, sender_name, subject, date, snippet, label_ids}.

matched.description: How many messages matched the query.

truncated.description: True when matched exceeded returned. A total over these rows counts `returned`, not `matched` — bind a headline total to `matched` and say "the most recent N of M". Use nextPageToken for the rest.

returned.description: How many came back. Every returned row is a full record; unreadable rows are not returned.

providedTools.description: Search messages by query (Gmail syntax); supports paging. Each result already carries id, thread_id, sender, sender_email, sender_name, subject, date and snippet. Bind them directly. Do NOT add a step to extract those fields; they are not in the message body.

providedTools.description: Fetch one message's parsed metadata (sender, subject, snippet, ids).
Estimated count of messages matching a query.
Add a label to a message (created if it doesn't exist).
Add and/or remove labels by name; remove INBOX to archive.
Add/remove labels across up to 1000 messages in one call (bulk trash: add TRASH; archive: remove INBOX).

_localNote: Studio can broker this. Only tools marked "local": true can be called — the rest are hosted-platform only.
